info.title: MICROSERVICE_PROD_Merchant Deactivation API
info.description: The Merchant Deactivation API allows businesses to deactivate a specific merchant record from their system by providing the unique merchant ID. This operation is essential for maintaining up-to-date records and ensuring compliance with business policies. Typically used by account managers or administrators, this API supports the management of merchant relationships and resources. By utilizing this endpoint, organizations can effectively manage their merchant database while retaining the ability to reinstate deactivated merchants if necessary.

delete.description: This endpoint allows the deletion of a merchant specified by the unique identifier. Once deleted, the merchant will no longer be available in the system. Ensure that the merchant ID provided is correct, as this action is irreversible.

requestBody.description: This request body is used to send a delete operation for the specified merchant. It should contain all necessary details required for the successful deletion of the merchant from the system.

DeleteMerchantByIdRequest.description: This schema represents the request body for the DELETE operation on the merchant identified by MER-800045.

metadata.description: Metadata related to the response including identifiers and timestamps.

DeleteMerchantByIdResponse_204.description: Response schema for DELETE operation indicating successful processing.

responseId.description: A unique identifier for the response.

correlationId.description: ID used to trace the request through the system.

generatedAt.description: Timestamp when the response was generated.

processingRegion.description: Region where the request was processed.

Metadata.description: Contains metadata information about the API response.

X-Endpoint-Id.description: A unique identifier for the endpoint that has processed the request.

X-Runtime-App.description: The name of the application that is currently running the operation.

bearerAuth.description: Authentication using a Bearer token. This scheme requires that clients provide a valid JSON Web Token (JWT) in the 'Authorization' header of their requests to access secure endpoints.
